subject: Persistent pipeline elongation impacting completions — urgent
messages:
From: Brian Lee <brian.lee@fasttrack.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: intermittent 500s and huge completion tails

Vanessa,

We started seeing a sustained spike in long-tail completions since ~08:40 PT this morning. Impact: session timeouts in our checkout flow and 502/504 errors — customers are reporting slow carts. Quick metrics from our side: p95 generation latency jumped from ~600ms to ~1.2s, p99 sits at ~18s and there are frequent timeouts. Error rate on /v1/complete is ~4.1% (was <0.2%).

Sample request IDs (from our side) that timed out: req_20280518_8a17, req_20280518_8a23, req_20280518_8a40. We attached a small log extract and a couple of requests for you.

We need an emergency mitigation and an ETA for full recovery — this is customer-impacting for our production checkout. Can we get an urgent sync?

-Brian
Brian Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, FastTrack Logistics
ops@fasttrack.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Brian Lee <brian.lee@fasttrack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent 500s and huge completion tails

Hi Brian — thanks for the heads up and the log snippets. I’m escalating this immediately and we’ve opened an incident (JIRA-OPS-1127). First things we’re doing now: 

- Spinning up a burst pool for FastTrack routes to relieve queued requests.
- Temporarily increasing per-route concurrency cap by 2x for your account to reduce queuing.
- Enabling fallback routing to the lower-latency model variant for short completions.

Ben/Stephanie — can you confirm the burst pool and concurrency change and post telemetry after the change?

Brian — can you keep the logs/IDs coming; we’re going to track correlated request_ids. I’ll update you in 15 minutes with initial telemetry.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0118

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: telemetry snapshot + preliminary root cause notes

Flagging telemetry we grabbed at 09:28 PT:
- Model route FT-route-502: concurrency cap hit (current cap = 80, incoming bursts briefly peaked at ~220 conns), queue length spiked to ~780 requests.
- KV-cache churn increased, resulting in repeated prefix loads and cold starts for many requests.
- Observed degraded kernel scheduling on one GPU host due to a large batch job from unrelated tenant at the same time (node gpu-4).
- Error signature: timeouts at service-proxy layer followed by 5xx from runtime when kqueue > 600.

Attachments: support_sla_snapshot.png (pre/post), fasttrack-sample-requests.log.txt (subset).

Immediate runbook we already executed:
1) Increase per-route concurrency cap to 200 and allocate burst pool (temporary).
2) Apply route weight to move 40% of traffic to the lower-memory model variant (gpt-large-compact) for requests with <256 tokens.
3) Drain heavy batch job off gpu-4 and reschedule to low-priority queue.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: concurrent pressure from a combination of unusually high short/fast requests (bunching at microsecond granularity) + one noisy neighbor batch causing GPU scheduling jitter + hot-prefix churn causing repeated cold KV loads. That combinatorial stack created queueing that pushed many requests into tail latency and subsequent proxy timeouts.

Ben — can you confirm the node drain status and whether KV eviction rates fell after the concurrency bump?

-Marissa

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Brian Lee <brian.lee@fasttrack.com>, Ops Team <ops@fasttrack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent 500s and huge completion tails

Brian — quick update: we applied the temporary mitigations at 09:36 PT. Initial numbers (09:36–09:58 window): p99 dropped from ~18s to ~3.2s and error rate fell from 4.1% to ~0.9%. Some residual tails remain for large-token requests.

Plan for the next 24 hours: 
- Short term (now–4h): keep burst pool and raised cap, continue using the lower-memory model for <256-token requests. Monitor for regressions.
- Medium term (24–72h): schedule permanent route configuration to increase steady-state capacity and add prefix-KV prewarm for FastTrack traffic.
- Long term (2–4 weeks): evaluate model variant pinning for critical routes and add telemetry-based auto-shed when noisy-neighbor patterns detected.

Can you join a 30-minute call at 11:00 PT for a quick handoff and to review logs? If 11:00 doesn’t work, propose a time.

We’ve attached the log extract and the pre/post snapshots. Apologies for the impact — we’ll keep you updated frequently until we’re back to baseline.

— Vanessa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exec loop: FastTrack service-impacting long-tail — sync + commercial ask

Looping in execs and ops. FastTrack is seeing a production-facing regression; Vanessa please confirm: current customer-visible errors and ETR.

Commercial note: they are asking about a short-term SLA credit and want a written ETR by EOD. Please prepare a brief (1-paragraph) operational summary + ETR for the leadership readout. We’ll sync at 12:00 PT to agree message and next steps.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Brian Lee <brian.lee@fasttrack.com>, Ops Team <ops@fasttrack.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent 500s and huge completion tails — next steps and ETR

Brian — follow-up from the 12:00 PT sync: current status is stable and close to baseline for short completions. Remaining items and ETR: 

- Action items completed: burst pool + concurrency cap increase; noisy neighbor batch drained; route weight applied to lower-memory model for short requests.
- Open work (in progress): prefix-KV prewarm for top-50 keys (ETA 6–8 hours), schedule configuration change for steady-state capacity (ETA 24 hours).
- Commercial/exec: draft credit proposal ready for review (Jonas), we will provide a written ETR and incident summary by EOD today.

We’ll keep monitoring and will escalate immediately for any regression. Thanks for your patience; apologies again for the outage window this morning.

Attachments: route-config-before-after.yml (snapshot of temporary config).

— Vanessa
